sourceChecks.claim: Live inspected AWS ELB traffic distribution and backend health scope, with nginx reverse proxy forwarding documentation; added proxy and operating costs are explicit tradeoffs.

Live inspected Azure L7 path/TLS visibility versus L4 transport capabilities. Followed AWS NLB documentation: an individual TCP connection remains on one target for its life, supporting the reused-request limitation.

Live inspected nginx round robin, least active connections and weighted request-share examples. These counts and configured shares are not live work measurements; unequal requests require measured choice.

Live inspected AWS periodic health intervals, consecutive thresholds and explicit fail-open when every target is unhealthy. A selected probe is a sample of its capability; already underway work is outside eligibility removal.

Live inspected ASP.NET web-farm shared data/cache requirements and node-local state limitations; nginx affinity stays on a preferred server except failure. Routing does not duplicate memory; shared storage is a separate dependency.

Live inspected ALB deregistration delay: stop new requests, retain draining time for in-flight work, early termination can yield errors. NLB connection-lifetime routing establishes why transport draining must also manage reused connections.

Previously live inspected AWS idempotent API atomic token-plus-effects requirement and stable caller identity. Same mechanism supports shared purchase result deduplication; Azure retry guidance supports bounded delay.

Live inspected Google overload discussion: requests have unequal resource costs; redirect only to capacity, reject excess gracefully and prevent cascades. AWS NLB multi-AZ reachable nodes/DNS behavior supports the need for a usable alternate entry path.
